references.text: The same chapter also mentions the number of Israelite warriors, four hundred thousand men with swords, confirming the size of the army.
The congregation sent twelve thousand warriors, showing the same military organization of Israel's tribal assembly.
Saul mustered the men of Israel at Bezek, three hundred thousand, demonstrating a similar military muster of the tribes.
Saul mustered the people and counted them: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, illustrating the same type of military census.
Describes how all Israel gathered as one man, from Dan to Be'er-Sheba, in the same assembly.
The leaders of the tribes are called 'chiefs' or 'principal men,' corresponding to the 'cornerstones' (pinnot) mentioned here.
Describes God's assembly (kehal) and who may participate in it; the same expression is used here.
The Israelites were counted by their families and ancestral houses, a similar census of the people.
